question: ‘Pax Silica’ is a US-led initiative aimed at securing global supply chains for AI semiconductors and critical minerals. It seeks to establish a reliable and robust ecosystem for key technologies in the AI era and hinges on coordinated action among allies and partners, selected on the basis of their role within the production chain.

The Government of the Philippines signed up to the US-led initiative in April 2026, agreeing to host a hub for mineral-processing and semiconductor-manufacturing in a move that will lead to the forced displacement of hundreds of small farmers and indigenous people.
The Commission has signed the ‘Pax Silica’ declaration on behalf of the EU, committing to cooperate with global partners to advance AI and supply chain security.

In light of the above, can the Commission explain how it intends to reconcile its involvement and cooperation in strategic frameworks such as ‘Pax Silica’ with the need to ensure that semiconductor and critical mineral sourcing projects do not undermine the rights of indigenous peoples, as enshrined in international standards?
